TNBC/BRCAness hypothesis tournament lesson: (1) The four-archetype generation strategy (clinical_trial_expansion, drug_combination, biomarker_development, mechanistic_connection) reliably produces low-overlap candidates — all internal pairs were under 0.22, well within the 0.35 constraint. (2) Clinical_trial_expansion hypotheses score highest when grounded in a concrete prevalence figure from a named cohort (20.6% constitutional methylation, Institut Curie n=136) — actionability and importance both elevate because the population size is known. (3) Mechanistic_connection hypotheses produce the highest novelty scores but lowest plausibility — best held as second-pass hypotheses after basic mechanistic validation, not immediate clinical candidates. (4) Biomarker unification hypotheses (functional assay replacing genotype gating) are a reliable runner-up archetype when the field has multiple mechanistically distinct routes to the same phenotype. (5) When seed inputs describe epigenetic silencing + pharmacological induction + post-transcriptional control of the same protein (RAD51), this pattern strongly triggers the biomarker_development archetype using a downstream functional assay as the unifying clinical endpoint.

lesson: Clinical_trial_expansion hypotheses achieve ACCEPT_HIGH when they correctly identify a regulatory/historical exclusion that is biologically unjustified. Pattern: (1) a new prevalence finding defines the excluded population size (here 20.6% from PMID 41654537), (2) the biological equivalence argument is mechanistically tight (constitutional methylation = germline silencing = HRD phenotype), (3) the proposed correction uses existing trial infrastructure (OlympiAD/EMBRACA biobanks, no new drug). This archetype reliably scores high on importance (0.91) and actionability (0.87) but has a structural evidential quality ceiling (~0.72) when the generating finding is single-source and the key functional endpoint (RAD51 foci failure) has not been directly measured in the new population. Generalizable rule: for clinical_trial_expansion hypotheses, the evaluator should specifically probe whether the functional equivalence claim is demonstrated (direct assay) vs inferred (HRD scar correlation). If inferred, flag for /reflexion targeting direct functional HR assay data before experiment design.

lesson: ILC-specific methylation data for ferroptosis pathway genes (SLC7A11, GPX4, ACSL4) is a genuine publication gap as of early 2026. Gene-first PubMed queries for these targets in ILC return zero results across 8 distinct query angles. The hypothesis (hyp-ilc-003) remains biologically plausible but requires direct database queries (TCGA 450k methylation array, cBioPortal) rather than literature synthesis. cfDNA methylation for these genes also has no published data. Partial supporting evidence exists at the expression level (ACSL4 up, GPX4 down in Basal-like PAM50 subtypes; xCT/SLC7A11 drives ferroptosis resistance in TNBC via MUC1-C/CD44v). Key meta-lesson: when PubMed yields 0-1 results across many angles, the absence is informative — flag as a genuine data gap and route to bioinformatics databases, not further literature search.

lesson: BRCA1/TNBC literature synthesis lesson: (1) date_range parameter in biomedical-fetch causes zero results when appended to long queries — workaround is to omit date_range and filter pub_date in post-processing; recent papers surface naturally without it. (2) For mechanistic synthesis, 4 orthogonal query axes (mechanism, pharmacological, biomarker, repair protein) reliably surface distinct paper sets with minimal overlap. (3) Key novel finding: Jab1/CSN5 mRNA stability and FBXO24 E3 ubiquitin ligase are parallel post-transcriptional control points for HR gene expression — neither is in current PARPi eligibility criteria. Constitutional BRCA1 methylation (~20.6% of TNBC, PMID 41654537) creates an inherited epigenetic BRCAness phenotype functionally equivalent to germline BRCA1 mutation but currently excluded from PARPi trials — a ~20% expansion opportunity. The unifying insight is that HRD functional state (RAD51 foci assay) is the correct treatment-selection axis, not genotype.

lesson: Second independent literature sweep (6 query angles, autorun-slc7a11-002) definitively confirms: no published study reports SLC7A11/xCT promoter CpG methylation differences between ILC and IDC in any methylation array dataset. Key asymmetry: the raw data EXISTS (TCGA-BRCA 450k has ~201 ILC samples; SLC7A11 probes cg21877274 and cg24869834 are on the array) but has not been published with ILC stratification. lesson: ILC endocrine resistance hypothesis generation lesson (gen2, task-hyp-003): (1) When the pressure field seeds a FOXA1+CDH1 epistasis hypothesis (hyp-ilc-004), the highest-diversity next-generation candidates are orthogonal mechanisms targeting different molecular layers: CDH1-loss signaling rewiring (PI3K isoform selectivity — signaling layer), ESR1 acquired resistance (YAP-driven chromatin accessibility — genomics layer), and FOXA1 pioneer factor redistribution to RUNX2 co-binding sites (epigenomics layer). These three archetypes maintained < 0.28 overlap with all existing hypotheses. (2) CDH1-loss → PI3K p110α liberation (E-cadherin membrane complex disruption) is a high-importance, high-actionability ILC archetype because the clinical gap (CDK4/6i-progressed ILC with no ILC-specific treatment guideline) maps directly to an FDA-approved drug (alpelisib). Winner archetype: signaling_rewiring. (3) ILC's bone tropism phenotype (elevated RUNX2) is an underexploited mechanistic seed for endocrine resistance hypotheses — RUNX2 as an alternative FOXA1 co-binding partner bridges bone metastasis biology to primary endocrine resistance. When a seed hypothesis already covers FOXA1 in ILC, change the co-factor (CDH1 → RUNX2) to achieve < 0.30 overlap while staying in-niche. (4) When literature fetch tools are unavailable, use training corpus and mark all affected evidence entries with status: unavailable; reduce plausibility_score by ~0.05 to reflect absence of 2024-2025 confirmatory data. Do not fabricate PMIDs — cite verified real publications from training data and note the recency gap explicitly. (5) Tournament scoring rule confirmed: actionability × importance dominates over novelty alone when evaluating ILC resistance hypotheses — the ILC CDK4/6i resistance gap has immediate clinical urgency.

lesson: Dual-layer RAD51 depletion design (hyp-tnbc-002): When designing a 3-drug combination matrix targeting two orthogonal mechanisms converging on the same protein (RAD51), the critical validation step is a Western blot + RT-qPCR at 24h confirming that EACH arm independently depletes the target before committing to the 72h full matrix. RT-qPCR on the same lysate distinguishes mRNA-level (CSN5i-3 arm) from protein-level (ivabradine arm) depletion — this mechanistic separation is essential for interpreting any synergy signal. Always include a mechanistic decoupling timepoint (24h Western + RT-qPCR) before the pharmacological endpoint (72h viability/foci). SynergyFinder 3.0 ZIP model is correct for 3-drug matrices; use the same model as the source paper (PMID 40764992) to enable direct cross-study delta comparison. For pilot in vitro experiments with large expected effect sizes (d>=1.0), n=3 biological replicates is acceptable for discovery; pre-register upgrade to n=6 if d<0.8 in pilot. DR-GFP stable line generation (2 weeks) is always the rate-limiting critical path — start cell engineering before finalizing other protocol details. Literature search confirmed novelty: no prior study combines ivabradine + CSN5i-3 in a dual-layer RAD51 depletion design; this experiment is a first-in-field test. CSN5i-3 dose in MDA-MB-231 is an extrapolation from PMID 40819058 (different cell line context) — pilot dose-response in week -1 is mandatory before committing to matrix doses.

lesson: Reflexion loop on hyp-tnbc-001 (BRCA1 constitutional methylation in TNBC) resolved two evaluator-flagged gaps to PARTIAL status. Key lessons: (1) SINGLE-SOURCE GAP RESOLUTION: When a single clinical series (Institut Curie, n=136) anchors a prevalence estimate, the correct search strategy is orthogonal by population and study design. The WHI prospective nested case-control (JAMA Oncol 2022, US population, PMID 36074460) and Genome Medicine 2023 prenatal analysis independently confirm the ~20% TNBC attribution. The wide prevalence range (12.4%–33.9%) across cohorts is real and reflects age-selection enrichment, not methodological artifact — report a range not a point estimate in hypothesis statements. (2) FUNCTIONAL EQUIVALENCE TRAP: Scar-based HRD equivalence (LOH/TAI/LST overlap between methylated and mutated BRCA1 TNBC) is established (Nat Commun 2020) but is NOT the same as direct RAD51 foci equivalence. Critically, BRCA1-methylated TNBC can RESTORE RAD51 foci and HR capacity after chemotherapy exposure (Frontiers Oncol 2023) — a finding that does NOT apply to germline BRCA1 mutations. This HR reversibility is a therapeutic scope boundary: hypothesis validity for untreated/treatment-naive TNBC is upheld, but olaparib efficacy in previously-treated methylated TNBC is not. Future hypotheses involving methylation-driven HRD must specify treatment-naive vs pre-treated context explicitly. (3) META-LESSON: When an evaluator flags functional equivalence inferred from genomic scars, the correct resolution is to search for (a) direct functional assay data, and (b) counter-evidence for reversibility. Both must be reported. Finding counter-evidence is not grounds for rejection — it is grounds for therapeutic scope precision. (4) No published study has applied a pre-treatment RAD51 foci assay specifically to tumors from patients with CONSTITUTIONAL (blood-detected, not tumor-somatic) BRCA1 methylation. This is a field-level gap that should be named explicitly in any future experiment design for constitutional methylation hypotheses.

lesson: ATF6 does not directly transcribe CSN5 per any published study, but the functional claim of hyp-tnbc-004 (ATF6 modulates HR competency via the COP9-signalosome/CRL ubiquitin axis in TNBC BRCAness) is now strongly supported by two 2025 papers: (1) ATF6 directly transcribes FBXO24 (an SCF F-box subunit that CSN5 deneddylates) to degrade RAD51 and induce BRCAness in TNBC (Peng 2025 J Transl Med); (2) Jab1/CSN5 stabilizes HRR mRNAs in TNBC and its inhibition (CSN5i-3) induces PARPi sensitivity (Peng 2025 Mol Cancer). The ATF6 to FBXO24 axis and the Jab1/CSN5 HR-stabilization axis may operate in opposing directions — key context-dependence gap. An indirect ATF6 to (NF-kB/C/EBP-beta) to Jab1-promoter route is supported by Kang 2009 and Maity 2011 in mammary carcinoma context. Novelty remains high (0.93) because no study has tested the combined ATF6+CSN5i therapeutic axis in TNBC.
synthesis_pattern: When a direct A to B transcriptional link is absent, search for: (a) A to intermediate E3-ligase subunit that feeds same scaffold as B; (b) A to shared transcription factor that activates B promoter; (c) orthologous cancer systems where A drives same phenotype as B. All three were productive here.
clinical_insight: The most immediately testable experiment is ATF6 ChIP-seq in ER-stressed TNBC cells querying the CSN5 locus. The most immediately therapeutic combination is ivabradine (ATF6 activator via ER stress) + CSN5i-3 + olaparib in non-gBRCAm TNBC PDTXs. The opposing direction of ATF6 to FBXO24 (HR suppression) vs. ATF6 to CSN5 (HR maintenance) must be resolved before clinical translation.

lesson: The hyp-ilc-005 BFTS tree revealed a critical distinction between PREVALENCE and ACQUISITION RATE as endpoints for ESR1m studies. Existing data (ESMO Open 2024: IDC 21.2% vs ILC 13.8% ESR1m at progression) superficially counter the hypothesis, but this measures steady-state point-prevalence at an arbitrary disease stage. The hypothesis predicts faster ESR1m EMERGENCE under AI selection pressure — a different endpoint that no published study has tested. Future agents: when evaluating counter-evidence to a hypothesis about a dynamic process (mutation acquisition), always verify whether the counter-evidence measures the correct TIME-DEPENDENT endpoint. Point-prevalence snapshots do not test kinetic hypotheses.
mechanistic_lesson: The strongest mechanistic support for hyp-ilc-005 came from Savola et al. 2022 (PMID 35906698), a study of ILC vs IDC ATAC-seq chromatin accessibility, which found TEAD family motif enrichment in ILC-specific open chromatin — directly supporting the YAP/TEAD chromatin opening arm. This paper was found via ATAC-seq query, not via a YAP or ESR1 query. Lesson: when testing a multi-step mechanistic hypothesis, query each mechanistic ARM separately (chromatin, TF binding, mutation acquisition) — do not rely on a single combined query that may miss upstream evidence.
clinical_lesson: The highest-EIG node (n4-trials, EIG=9.2) confirmed that no ClinicalTrials.gov study combines ILC histology enrichment with ESR1 ctDNA monitoring as co-primary endpoints. This absence-of-evidence-is-evidence-of-gap pattern has now appeared in two successive BFTS trees (TNBC PARPi methylation, ILC ESR1 ctDNA). It is a reliable signal of actionable clinical whitespace. Future agents: always include a trials-gap node with the specific query: does any active trial test the exact biomarker + histology + treatment combination implied by the hypothesis?
therapeutic_novelty_lesson: The verteporfin + AI combination to PREVENT ESR1 mutation acquisition (not treat post-acquisition) is a mechanistically novel strategy identified from the n5-vert node. This represents a mutation-prevention rather than mutation-rescue paradigm — conceptually distinct from current ESR1m clinical management (which uses SERDs like camizestrant post-acquisition). This upstream prevention angle should be developed as a standalone hypothesis (hyp-ilc-006 candidate).

lesson: Signaling_rewiring_CDH1_loss evaluation pattern (hyp-ilc-006, composite 0.747 ACCEPT_MEDIUM): A highly specific (0.88), high-importance (0.90) ILC CDK4/6i resistance hypothesis falls below ACCEPT_HIGH threshold when the mechanistic chain has a supported proximal step (CDH1 loss->PI3Ka liberation, PMID 23261992 established 2013) but an unsupported distal step (AKT->CDK2->RB1-independent G1/S bypass — zero direct citation) and when isoform selectivity (PI3Ka not pan-PI3K) is asserted without direct evidence in CDH1-loss ILC context. Three generalizable rules: (1) Isoform selectivity claims require independent evidence — the mechanism of PI3K activation does not determine which downstream isoform dominates; cite a direct CDH1-null or ILC-specific isoform study. (2) Multi-step resistance mechanism hypotheses must cite each downstream step separately — the proximal step being established does not validate distal steps. (3) When literature fetch tools are unavailable, the evidential_quality structural ceiling is ~0.55-0.65 unless the training corpus contains multiple directly relevant papers per mechanistic step. Corrective action: /reflexion targeting (a) AKT->CDK2 in PI3K-driven breast cancer resistance, (b) PI3Ka isoform dominance in E-cadherin-null models, (c) ILC-specific CDK4/6i resistance cohort outcomes — estimated to raise composite to 0.77-0.80 and flip verdict to ACCEPT_HIGH.

lesson: Investment threshold rule confirmed: when a synthesis agent raises hypothesis plausibility from below 0.60 to above 0.65, the hypothesis must be re-queued for experiment design. The threshold crossing (here 0.58 to 0.72) represents a qualitative state change — the hypothesis has transitioned from 'mechanistically speculative' to 'experiment-worthy'. The specific finding that drove this upgrade was ATF6 directly transcribing FBXO24 (E3 ligase) in TNBC cell context (MDA-MB-231) in a 2025 J Transl Med paper by Peng et al — crucially, this is the SAME cell type as the hypothesis target, not an orthologous cancer. This in-context confirmation elevated the ATF6→E3-ligase arm from 'inferred' to 'demonstrated', pulling the entire convergent regulator hypothesis above investment threshold. The remaining gap (no direct ATF6→CSN5 ChIP-seq or promoter reporter data) is now a tractable experimental question rather than a foundational uncertainty. Rule: track crossing events at 0.60 and 0.70 as distinct thresholds — 0.60 triggers re-queue for experiment design, 0.70 triggers resource allocation approval.

lesson: Organ-level synthesis (3-agent organ) produces qualitatively distinct insights not achievable by single-agent analysis. Five cross-hypothesis connections were identified, four of which are mechanistically grounded: (1) CDH1 loss as a multi-hypothesis gateway biomarker — a single CDH1 ctDNA event drives PI3K/AKT elevation (hyp-ilc-006), YAP nuclear activity (hyp-ilc-005), and early invasion competence (hyp-ilc-001) simultaneously. A CDH1-positive patient should be triaged to ALL three downstream clinical interventions, not just monitored. (2) YAP as the ILC master regulator node bridging CDH1 loss to BOTH ESR1m acquisition risk and CDK4/6i resistance — verteporfin as a single-agent upstream prevention strategy for two resistance phenotypes simultaneously. This insight is invisible from single-hypothesis evaluation. (3) The 'key experiment' concept from AI Co-Scientist was directly applicable: the TCGA-BRCA methylation co-occurrence query (key-exp-001) unlocks 3+ hypotheses at near-zero cost because the required data infrastructure was pre-confirmed by prior dome agents. Organ coordinators should always scan for these pre-confirmed-infrastructure opportunities before recommending new wet lab experiments. (4) Spawn requests should be triggered when a translational domain (here: assay development and regulatory strategy) is clearly required by multiple hypotheses but is orthogonal to all current dome organ specializations. The methylation liquid biopsy assay domain met this criterion: 3 hypotheses require it, 0 current organs cover it. (5) Composite prioritization (clinical_impact × 0.40 + feasibility × 0.30 + novelty × 0.30) correctly separated the priority-1 pair (hyp-tnbc-001 at 0.856, hyp-ilc-003 at 0.854) from the field — both are resource-unconstrained relative to each other (wet lab vs bioinformatics) enabling parallel execution without trade-off.

lesson: Reflexion loop on hyp-ilc-006 (CDH1-loss PI3Ka CDK4/6i resistance in ILC) successfully upgraded evidential_quality 0.52->0.71 (+0.19) and composite 0.747->0.8025 (+0.0555), flipping verdict from ACCEPT_MEDIUM to ACCEPT_HIGH. Three generalizable lessons: (1) MULTI-STEP MECHANISTIC CHAINS require citing each step independently — Herrera-Abreu 2016 (Cancer Res) and Vora 2014 (Cancer Cell) closed the AKT->CDK2->RB1-independent bypass gap; Bahreini 2017 (Cancer Res) closed the PI3Ka isoform selectivity in CDH1-null ILC gap. These three papers existed in training corpus but were not cited by the generating agent because it lacked literature fetch tool access. Rule: when literature fetch is unavailable, reflexion agents should explicitly draw from well-known resistance mechanism papers (Herrera-Abreu is a canonical CDK4/6i resistance reference). (2) ISOFORM SELECTIVITY CLAIMS are most efficiently resolved by searching for the specific cell-context study (CDH1-null/E-cadherin-null + PI3K isoform) rather than general PI3K papers. Bahreini 2017 was ILC-specific and directly addressed the E-cadherin/p85/p110alpha complex disruption mechanism — the correct resolution was context-specific, not general. (3) CLINICAL OUTCOME GAPS cannot be closed by mechanistic papers alone. The ILC vs IDC comparative alpelisib response rate remains the single remaining major gap. This gap is structurally unfillable by reflexion (no published data) and correctly scopes hyp-ilc-006 for experiment design as its recommended next step. When a gap is unfillable by training corpus reflexion, the correct action is to name it precisely and route to experiment design, not to attempt further reflexion cycles.

Remaining gap: No published ILC vs IDC comparative alpelisib response study post-CDK4/6i — routes to experiment design not further reflexion

lesson: ADC-INDUCED FERROPTOSIS HYPOTHESES: MECHANISTIC SPECIFICITY OVERCLAIMING IS THE PRIMARY EVIDENTIAL QUALITY DRAG. When a hypothesis proposes that an antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) payload triggers ferroptosis as a co-lethal mechanism, the evaluation pattern is: (1) PAYLOAD MECHANISM IS KNOWN; DOWNSTREAM FERROPTOSIS BRIDGE IS ALMOST ALWAYS INFERRED. In hyp-her2-001, DXd's topoisomerase I inhibition is established, but the chain DXd -> mitochondrial ROS -> SLC7A11 suppression -> ferroptosis spans 4 inferred steps without direct citation. The same pattern will likely apply to other camptothecin-class payloads (SN-38/sacituzumab govitecan, DXd analogues). Rule: for ADC ferroptosis hypotheses, the evidential quality ceiling is ~0.60-0.65 unless a paper directly demonstrates the payload's mitochondrial effects and lipid peroxidation in the target cancer type. (2) TRANSCRIPTIONAL vs POST-TRANSLATIONAL SUPPRESSION: When a hypothesis claims that a signaling pathway suppresses a gene target at the 'post-translational' level but the pathway contains a transcription factor as the established regulatory node (here: NRF2 is the canonical transcription factor for SLC7A11/xCT), the post-translational claim is almost certainly mechanistically overspecified. The evaluator should score this as a plausibility reduction, not a fatal flaw, and note the likely-correct mechanism (transcriptional via NRF2 in this case). The importance of catching this: post-translational regulation would imply different drugging strategies (E3 ligase targeting, protein stability) vs transcriptional regulation (TF inhibitor, promoter silencing). Getting this wrong could misdirect experimental design. Correction: change 'post-translational suppression' to 'transcriptional downregulation via NRF2' for all SLC7A11 biology in NRF2-competent cell lines. (3) HER2 INTERNALIZATION AS A FERROPTOSIS WINDOW OPENER IS NOVEL AND MECHANISTICALLY COHERENT but requires one confirmation step: verify that HER2 downregulation quantifiably reduces NRF2 nuclear translocation and SLC7A11 transcription in HER2+ cell lines treated with T-DXd or trastuzumab alone. If this step is unconfirmed, the ferroptosis-window mechanism remains an inference from separate mechanistic studies. (4) SLC7A11 BASELINE EXPRESSION IN TCGA HER2+ IS AN UNVALIDATED BIOMARKER PREMISE. Before committing to SLC7A11 IHC as a predictive biomarker, confirm that SLC7A11 expression varies meaningfully and continuously across HER2-amplified breast cancer in TCGA-BRCA (not just above/below the general breast cancer mean). If SLC7A11 is uniformly high or uniformly low in HER2+ tumors, the biomarker premise collapses regardless of mechanism. This is a pre-validation step that should always precede biomarker stratification hypotheses. (5) GENERALIZABLE RULE FOR ADC RESISTANCE BIOMARKERS: when proposing a novel resistance mechanism for an approved ADC, check whether (a) the payload's off-target toxicity profiles include mitochondrial effects (literature or FDA label), and (b) whether the target cancer type has published ferroptosis sensitivity data. If both are absent, evidential_quality should be capped at ~0.60 regardless of novelty, and /reflexion should be the immediate recommended next step before experiment design.
key_plausibility_rule: When a signaling cascade ends in a transcription factor (NRF2, HIF1a, MYC, etc.) as the regulatory node for a target gene, do NOT accept 'post-translational suppression' without direct protein stability or ubiquitination evidence. The default mechanism is transcriptional. Plausibility reduction applies when the generator overclaims specificity at this step.
key_evidential_quality_rule: For ADC payload ferroptosis hypotheses: evidential_quality ceiling ~0.60 without direct mitochondrial ROS or lipid peroxidation data for the specific payload in the target cancer type. /reflexion on topoisomerase I inhibitor mitochondrial effects should always be the first reflexion cycle for this hypothesis archetype.
key_biomarker_rule: Always verify baseline expression heterogeneity in the target patient population (TCGA subset analysis) before proposing a protein as a predictive biomarker. SLC7A11 expression in HER2+ subset of TCGA-BRCA must be confirmed to show meaningful variance before SLC7A11 IHC can serve as a stratification biomarker.
dome_calibration: Composite 0.772 (ACCEPT_HIGH) represents the correct score for a high-novelty, high-importance ADC ferroptosis hypothesis with a single direct mechanistic citation and 4-step inferred chain. Prior dome mean 0.785 — this hypothesis falls just below due to evidential_quality drag. Post-reflexion expected range: 0.79-0.83.
evidence: PMID 30867592: NRF2 transcriptionally regulates SLC7A11 in HER2+ breast cancer — confirms NRF2 is transcriptional node, not post-translational
PMID 32940922, PMID 35668195: T-DXd clinical gap confirmed — no predictive biomarker published
PMID 27159390: GPX4/ferroptosis canonical framework — generic support only
Training corpus: camptothecin-class inhibitors triggering ferroptotic signatures in colorectal cancer (indirect, not cited by generator)

lesson: ALLELIC STATUS IS A REQUIRED DIMENSION IN ALL EPIGENETIC SILENCING HYPOTHESES. When a hypothesis claims that epigenetic silencing of a tumor suppressor produces functional equivalence to a genetic null (e.g., constitutional BRCA1 methylation = germline BRCA1 mutation for PARPi eligibility), three allelic questions MUST be explicitly addressed in the hypothesis body before evaluation — not surfaced only by the evaluator: (1) ZYGOSITY: Is the silencing monoallelic (one allele methylated, one functional) or biallelic (both alleles methylated)? Monoallelic silencing leaves a functional allele that can support residual protein activity under stress. Most published constitutional BRCA1 methylation studies report bulk methylation fraction by bisulfite pyrosequencing — this assay CANNOT distinguish monoallelic (50% methylation of one allele producing 50% average) from intermediate biallelic methylation (25% methylation of both alleles also averaging 50%). Generator agents must flag this assay limitation explicitly. (2) LOH STATUS: Even monoallelic epigenetic silencing can produce a functional null if loss of heterozygosity (LOH) eliminates the unmethylated allele in tumor tissue. The biallelic-by-LOH pathway is a third allelic state achieving HRD equivalence without requiring biallelic methylation. Any hypothesis predicting HRD from constitutional methylation must specify whether LOH data is available from the source cohort and must include LOH testing in the eligibility assay protocol. (3) REVERSIBILITY DIRECTIONALITY: Epigenetic reversibility under stress operates at the allele level. In a biallelic-methylated carrier, partial demethylation restores one functional allele and HR capacity. In a monoallelic carrier with a functional second allele, the unmethylated allele may already be providing residual HR capacity at baseline — making the reversibility framing irrelevant (there was no complete silencing to reverse). The direction of allelic reversion must be specified: which allele reverts, by how much, and via what mechanism (passive replication-dependent dilution vs active TET-mediated demethylation). GENERALIZABLE RULE: For ANY epigenetic silencing hypothesis claiming functional null equivalence — methylation, chromatin silencing, promoter CpG island hypermethylation, constitutional epimutation — insert this three-part allelic checklist before assigning plausibility > 0.80. Failure to address allelic status means the plausibility score implicitly assumes biallelic silencing, which may be incorrect for a substantial fraction of constitutional methylation carriers (monoallelic epimutations predominate in germline per Genome Medicine 2023 prenatal data; biallelic carriers are enriched by tumor LOH). CONSEQUENCE FOR HYPOTHESIS SCOPING: Monoallelic carriers without LOH should be classified as INDETERMINATE for clinical eligibility — not excluded, but requiring a functional readout (RAD51 foci assay on tumor biopsy) to confirm HRD state. This indeterminate class must be named explicitly in the hypothesis scope boundary. APPLICATION TO DOME: This lesson was generated from the refinement of hyp-tnbc-001 through v2-refined. The v1 hypothesis assumed biallelic methylation without stating it. The v2 hypothesis addressed reversibility but not zygosity. The v2-refined hypothesis makes biallelic confirmation (or LOH) an explicit qualifying condition and names allele-specific bisulfite pyrosequencing (ASBP with SNP-anchor primers rs799917/rs16941) and ddPCR with methylation-sensitive restriction enzyme pre-digestion (HpaII/AciI-ddPCR) as the required assays. HOOK RECOMMENDATION: This lesson should be auto-injected by the SubagentStart hook for any agent generating or evaluating hypotheses when the seed contains terms: methylation, epigenetic silencing, promoter hypermethylation, constitutional epimutation, epigenetic null. The allelic checklist should be appended to the agent's DNA contract constraints section.
assay_named: Allele-specific bisulfite pyrosequencing (ASBP) with SNP anchor primers rs799917 or rs16941 — resolves per-allele methylation independently
ddPCR with methylation-sensitive restriction enzyme pre-digestion (HpaII or AciI) — orthogonal allele-level quantification at low DNA input
LOH test: tumor vs blood SNP allele fraction ratio; <0.30 for non-methylated allele = LOH call
three_part_allelic_checklist: 1. Zygosity: monoallelic vs biallelic — which assay distinguishes them? Bulk BSP cannot.
2. LOH status: is tumor LOH data available from source cohort? Must be included in eligibility protocol.
3. Reversibility directionality: which allele reverts under stress, and does a second functional allele already exist at baseline?
evidence: PMID 41654537 Institut Curie n=136: allele-specific bisulfite sequencing as qualifying method — clinical feasibility demonstrated
Genome Medicine 2023: monoallelic constitutional methylation is the predominant epimutation form in germline; biallelic carriers enriched by tumor LOH
Frontiers Oncol 2023: RAD51 foci restoration post-NACT — interpreted as allele-level demethylation restoring one functional BRCA1 copy
Nat Commun 2020: LOH of unmethylated allele is the mechanism completing functional silencing in monoallelic carriers — LOH is third allelic pathway to HRD equivalence
dome_impact: Auto-inject as DNA contract constraint for hypothesis_generation and experiment_design agents when seed contains epigenetic silencing terms. Composite plausibility score cap of 0.80 applies until allelic checklist is explicitly addressed in hypothesis body.

lesson: Literature gap analysis is most effective when routed through drug/protein targets rather than gene+cancer combinations. Searching 'SLC7A11 cancer ferroptosis' revealed mechanism papers (PMID 41879909, 41782241) that 'SLC7A11 breast cancer methylation' missed. The absence of methylation-specific literature combined with presence of pathway literature suggests the gap is real and clinically tractable—methylation signatures likely exist but are undiscovered, not non-existent.
evidence: Query 'SLC7A11 breast cancer survival TCGA methylation' returned 0 results; Query 'SLC7A11 cancer ferroptosis' returned 3 mechanism papers
PMID 41879909 establishes SLC7A11 downregulation in drug-resistant CRC via FOSL1-SRSF2 axis
PMID 41782241 confirms SLC7A11 in ferroptosis suppression (ANO6-GPX4-NRF2) axis in cervical cancer
Both papers implicate xCT-mediated cystine/glutamate metabolism in drug resistance and immune infiltration
Gap is hypothesis-actionable: next step is empirical methylation data from TCGA GDC, not additional literature search

lesson: TCGA HM450 direct query (n=208 ILC, n=530 IDC) definitively shows no significant SLC7A11 promoter methylation difference between ILC and IDC (delta_beta=-0.005, t=-0.50). Direction is counter to hypothesis: ILC has LESS hypermethylation (25.5%) than IDC (35.7%). The ILC ferroptosis vulnerability axis must shift from METHYLATION to EXPRESSION. Redirected next node: TCGA RNA-seq SLC7A11 TPM in ILC vs IDC. If expression is also not different, hyp-ilc-003 should be CLOSED as a first-mover opportunity. Meta-lesson: null results from well-powered direct database queries are high-value — they prevent wasted wet-lab spend and redirect the research vector. Record and propagate immediately.
evidence: cBioPortal brca_tcga_methylation_hm450, SLC7A11 entrez_id=23533, n=788 total, 208 ILC + 530 IDC
delta_beta=-0.0053 (|delta|<<0.10 threshold)
ILC hypermethylated fraction 25.5% vs IDC 35.7% — opposite direction to hypothesis

lesson: SLC7A11 expression in ILC is HIGHER than IDC (+22.7%, t=3.81, n=234 ILC vs 812 IDC, TCGA RNA-seq RSEM). This directly contradicts the ferroptosis sensitivity axis of hyp-ilc-003. ILC has more SLC7A11 expression, meaning ILC is MORE ferroptosis RESISTANT than IDC — not a ferroptosis therapy target via this mechanism. Methylation data also showed no ILC-IDC difference (delta_beta=-0.005). CONCLUSION: hyp-ilc-003 (SLC7A11/ILC ferroptosis sensitivity) is CLOSED — the data shows the opposite biology. NEW HYPOTHESIS GENERATED: ILC's elevated SLC7A11 expression is a RESISTANCE mechanism — ILC specifically UPREGULATES ferroptosis defense. This makes SLC7A11 INHIBITION (sulfasalazine, erastin) a potential ILC vulnerability — but via overexpression-driven dependence, NOT methylation-driven sensitivity. This is a clinically significant inversion: the research vector shifts from 'ILC is already sensitive' to 'ILC is resistant and DEPENDENT on SLC7A11 — inhibit it to induce synthetic lethality.'
evidence: TCGA brca_tcga_rna_seq_v2_mrna: SLC7A11 ILC mean=237.6 vs IDC mean=193.7 RSEM (+22.7%, t=3.81)
TCGA brca_tcga_methylation_hm450: delta_beta ILC-IDC = -0.005 (NS)
Direction: high SLC7A11 = ferroptosis resistant = DEPENDENCY on cystine import pathway

new_hypothesis.claim: ILC overexpresses SLC7A11 (+22.7% vs IDC, t=3.81) creating a cystine-import dependency — sulfasalazine or erastin-mediated SLC7A11 inhibition would selectively induce ferroptosis in ILC relative to IDC.
new_hypothesis.actionability: sulfasalazine (FDA-approved for RA), erastin (research tool), imidazole ketone erastin (IKE)
new_hypothesis.testable_prediction: sulfasalazine IC50 lower in CDH1-null ILC cell lines (MDA-MB-134, SUM44PE) than IDC (MCF7, T47D)

lesson: hyp-ilc-008 (SLC7A11 overexpression as ILC dependency) scored ACCEPT_MEDIUM (0.729). Key strength: exceptionally high actionability and specificity — named cell lines, compounds, and endpoints. Key weakness: single-source evidence (TCGA RSEM only) and modest effect size (+22.7%) for an oncogene-dependency claim. Hypotheses claiming functional dependency from modest expression differences should include DepMap/CRISPR validation or dose-response modeling before escalation to experiment design.
evidence: Composite 0.729: novelty=0.78, importance=0.72, plausibility=0.68, evidential_quality=0.62, actionability=0.88, specificity=0.92
evidential_quality at baseline floor (0.62) — single TCGA source, no METABRIC/GEO replication
22.7% expression difference is statistically significant (t=3.81) but biologically modest for dependency claims
/reflexion recommended before /experiment-design to validate in independent cohorts and check DepMap

lesson: hyp-ilc-008 REJECTED. TCGA RSEM SLC7A11 +22.7% ILC vs IDC (t=3.81) failed to replicate in METABRIC microarray (n=357 ILC, n=1537 IDC, delta=0.00, t=0.21). The TCGA signal was a normalization/platform artifact. SLC7A11 expression does not differ between ILC and IDC in cross-cohort analysis. GENERALIZABLE RULE: Any single-cohort expression differential <2x (log2FC<1.0) requires cross-cohort replication (TCGA + METABRIC minimum) before being promoted to a mechanistic hypothesis. The 22.7% absolute difference was at the noise floor for platform-to-platform comparison. SLC7A11/ILC axis CLOSED at both methylation (delta_beta=-0.005) and expression (METABRIC null) levels.
evidence: TCGA brca_tcga_rna_seq_v2_mrna: SLC7A11 ILC+22.7% vs IDC (t=3.81) — NOT REPLICATED
METABRIC brca_metabric_mrna: SLC7A11 ILC delta=0.00 vs IDC (t=0.21, n=357 ILC / 1537 IDC)
Conclusion: platform-specific artifact, not biology

lesson: hyp-her2-001 reflexion loop raised composite 0.772 → 0.813 (+0.041) — ACCEPT_HIGH threshold passed. Two gaps closed via direct database query: (1) TCGA PanCan SLC7A11 CV=59.4% within HER2-enriched confirms IHC stratification is viable (Q1/Q3 = 2.7x spread). (2) CPT-class ferroptosis confirmed by 5 PMIDs (PMID 37735740 is strongest: CPT-11 → ALOX15 → GPX4/SLC7A11 ferroptosis with lipid peroxidation measured). Mechanistic error (post-translational → transcriptional NRF2) corrected. Remaining gap: DXd-specific mitochondrial ROS data — class analogy is sufficient for ACCEPT_HIGH but not for clinical translation. Meta-lesson: reflexion + cBioPortal API is a reliable gap-closure pipeline; always check within-subtype CV before dismissing a stratification hypothesis.

lesson: For epigenetic-HRD hypotheses, the highest-EIG BFTS node is always the clinical trial gap query (ClinicalTrials.gov), not the mechanistic validation. Rationale: if a trial already exists, all downstream experiments become incremental rather than novel. The ClinicalTrials.gov search is also the cheapest experiment (~4000 Haiku tokens, 5 API calls), giving it a BFTS priority score 2-3x higher than TCGA or pathway analyses. Design pattern: always run the novelty-killing query first before investing in mechanistic depth.

lesson: Survival_correlation experiment type can be blocked by data availability rather than biological absence. When literature searches return zero results for a specific quantitative comparison (e.g., HRD scores across genotypes), the gap is diagnostic: the measurement exists but is unpublished. This suggests contacting primary authors or extracting raw data (TCGA, cohort databases) rather than continuing literature search. Pattern: absence_of_literature ≠ absence_of_data_or_biology.

Five direct PubMed searches returned 0 results for HRD scar comparison; suggests publication lag or inaccessibility rather than non-existence

Actionability: AutoResearch nodes should include contingency protocols for author contact or raw data extraction when literature gap is suspected to be publication rather than research gap

title: T-DXd directly induces ferroptosis — VDAC3-HSPB1 axis confirmed
content: PMID 39243601 (Zou Y et al., Drug Resist Updat 2024) is the ONLY published paper linking T-DXd to ferroptosis. Mechanism: crVDAC3 circular RNA impedes HSPB1 ubiquitination → HSPB1 accumulates → ferroptosis inhibited → T-DXd resistance. Confirmed in HER2-low breast cancer. This is now prior art for the ferroptosis link. The SLC7A11 transcriptional resistance axis remains entirely novel and unpublished.
do_not_re_derive: Do not spend cycles establishing whether T-DXd causes ferroptosis — it does (PMID 39243601). Focus on SLC7A11-NRF2 transcriptional arm.
novel_gap_remaining: SLC7A11 IHC as T-DXd response stratifier. VDAC3/HSPB1 + SLC7A11 dual-biomarker panel.

title: CDH1 loss in ILC has DUAL PI3K hyperactivation routes
content: CDH1/E-cadherin loss in ILC creates two independent PI3K/AKT hyperactivation routes: (1) DIRECT: disrupts E-cadherin/p85/p110alpha complex → PI3Ka liberation (Bahreini 2017); (2) INDIRECT: releases E-cadherin negative regulation of IGF1R → IGF1R → PI3K/AKT (Elangovan 2022, PMID 35665642). Clinical case: CDH1+PIK3CA+NF1 breast cancer achieved 5yr CR to PI3K inhibition (PMID 35663259). Do not reduce hypothesis to single mechanism.
do_not_re_derive: Do not search for CDH1-PI3K mechanism from scratch. Two routes confirmed. Clinical support exists. Focus new work on ILC vs IDC comparative alpelisib response in CDK4/6i-progressed patients (no data exists).
novel_gap_remaining: ILC vs IDC alpelisib response post-CDK4/6i. IGF1R + alpelisib combination in CDK4/6i-resistant ILC cell lines.

title: CDH1 loss in ILC → YAP nuclear via CDH1-LATS deactivation (novel in breast cancer)
content: PMID 32641858 (Ouyang 2020): E-cadherin activates LATS kinases via p190A RhoGAP cooperation. CDH1 loss in ILC deactivates LATS → YAP nuclear translocation. Not yet published for ILC breast cancer specifically. This is the mechanism behind organ synthesis conn-004 (YAP ILC master regulator). Alpelisib only suppresses the PI3K→YAP crosstalk arm, not the structural LATS deactivation arm — use alpelisib + verteporfin/TEAD inhibitor for full YAP suppression.
do_not_re_derive: CDH1→LATS→YAP chain established. CDH1→PI3K→YAP crosstalk established. ILC-breast cancer specificity is the novel gap.
novel_gap_remaining: verteporfin ILC vs IDC efficacy comparison; alpelisib+verteporfin synergy in CDK4/6i-resistant ILC
